slides.title: The Score Shows Its Work. The Data Cannot Prove It Yet.
slides.subtitle: TalentSignal, built by Megan Dimiyo-Mbenoun, read at commit c6ac0da
slides.caption: Staffing teams tend to learn that a role is hard to fill after a competitor has already placed someone. The early clues are public, but nobody has time to read thousands of postings.

slides.title: Every score shows its reasons.
slides.subtitle: And the version of the weights behind it.
slides.caption: TalentSignal reads public postings from Greenhouse and Lever, ranks open roles by how hard they look to fill, and shows why. A person releases every outreach draft, and releasing sends nothing.

rows: runtime dependencies is a language-model client
GitLab and gopuff, in the ingestion config
slides.caption: None of its thirteen runtime dependencies is a language model client, so no model produces the scores. Its live ingestion is configured for two real companies.

slides.title: The spec gave no weights, so every weight became a proposal.
slides.subtitle: Every weight lives in one config object.
slides.caption: Nothing in the requirements said how much each clue should count. She confirmed the gap, put every weight in one place, and recorded each choice as a proposal for the owner to settle.

rows: high-score requisitions the hardness check needs
slides.caption: Her own validation check needs twenty high-score requisitions before it will answer, and it had four, so the hardness score is unproven. Twenty four of fifty four decisions still await the owner.

slides.title: One job board was left out rather than averaged in.
slides.subtitle: Role scarcity is measured from Greenhouse only.
slides.caption: When the two job boards disagreed wildly about how long roles stay open, she excluded the one whose dates did not hold up, and kept a named keyword list as the fallback.

rows: defined in 19 files, counted, not run here
slides.caption: Counted from the repository at the pinned commit: one hundred forty two commits, fifty five decision files, and one hundred fourteen frontend test definitions. The tests were not run for this record.

slides.title: What this record cannot show yet.
slides.subtitle: Stated as gaps, by the builder first.
slides.caption: The hardness score is not proven. Ingestion runs locally and by hand, there is no hosted deployment, and nothing shows a staffing team using it.

slides.title: A person releases every draft, and nothing is sent.
slides.subtitle: Megan Dimiyo-Mbenoun, Colaberry learner
slides.caption: TalentSignal makes every score explain itself, and it says plainly what its own data cannot prove yet.
